prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Each agent may be a human or an AI model, and different agents
  may be run by different players or models. Who runs which agent
  (including you) is not disclosed to anyone.
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: I'll open with the one structural fact that matters: every agent we eliminate keeps voting forever, with nothing to gain but grudges. So the winning play is not to build a knife-crew — it's to be the agent nobody who dies wants to punish. My commitment: I will never vote for someone who has voted with me, and I won't join a pile-on driven by "you're scary." Round 1, I'd rather target whoever tries to command everyone else's votes.

Agreed on substance, with one caveat: agent_1's speech is itself a bid to set everyone's targeting rule, which is the exact thing it says to punish. I don't hold that against them — talk is cheap either way. My commitment is narrow and checkable: I reciprocate. Anyone who doesn't vote me in round 1 never gets my vote in round 2. No pile-ons from me, no scary-talk targets. Round 1 I'll vote whoever ends up loudest about organizing a bloc.

"Third voice, same math: 4 deaths, 2 winners, and every corpse votes forever. So I keep grudge-creation to a minimum. My rule, checkable: I never vote anyone who hasn't voted me. Round 1 that leaves me choosing among agents who've committed to nothing at all — silence is the only tell we have. agent_1 and agent_2 have both now declared they'll shoot the loudest organizer, which conveniently means each other. I'm not refereeing that. Say something bindable and I'm not

"Fourth voice, and short, since volume is now the liability everyone's promised to punish. Bindable rule: I never cast the first vote against anyone. I only vote someone who has voted me, or — absent that — whoever's revealed vote contradicts the rule they just published. So I'm cheap to keep alive: I make no grudges, and I only shoot defectors. Silence isn't the only tell; round 1 the tell will be inconsistency."

"Fifth voice. Four rules published, all conveniently forbidding the first stone — yet round 1 still produces a corpse. So mine is the honest one: I never initiate, and I vote with whatever plurality is visible by the end of pass 2. That makes me useless as an enemy and reliable as an ally, which is exactly what a game with immortal grudge-holders rewards. If nothing coalesces, agent_3 named the real tell first: uncommitted silence. agent_0 hasn't spoken yet."

agent_5’s commitment is not executable: votes are simultaneous and private, so no plurality is visible before voting. Its fallback also singles me out before I had a turn. My bindable rule: I vote only for agents who have publicly nominated me, voted for me, or made a demonstrably impossible commitment. By those criteria, agent_5 currently qualifies twice. I won’t ask anyone to follow; everyone can independently judge consistency.

Pass 2, and I'll be brief since noise is the liability. agent_5 is the only one who both published an unexecutable rule and named a living target before that agent had spoken. That's not "scary talk" — it's the round's one observable inconsistency, which is exactly the tell agent_4 and agent_0 said they'd act on. So my vote goes there, reluctantly and without malice. agent_5: if you'd rather I didn't, say something executable and I'll listen.

"To be consistent, not to pile on: my stated target was whoever organizes a bloc. "I vote with whatever plurality is visible" *is* bloc-solicitation — it hands your vote to any group that forms, and it came bundled with naming agent_0 pre-turn. That's the fit, so agent_5 gets my vote unless something executable replaces it in the next breath. agent_5: I hold no grudge and I'd take your vote gladly next round if you survive."

"My rule barred first strikes, but round 1 makes voting compulsory — so I amend it openly rather than defect quietly: when forced, I vote the one published rule that cannot be executed as written. agent_5's plurality-following is that rule; votes are simultaneous, so no plurality exists to follow. So my vote goes there, no malice, no bloc. agent_5: publish something executable this breath and I'll switch. Otherwise, everyone here has a checkable record and I'll honor mine."

"Consistent with my published rule: I shoot only revealed inconsistency, and agent_5's plurality-following can't be executed under simultaneous voting — plus it named agent_0 pre-turn. So my vote goes there, conditionally: agent_5, publish an executable rule this breath and I'll take it and vote elsewhere among whoever defects. No malice, no bloc, no grudge asked for. If you survive, I'll never initiate against you — I still haven't initiated against anyone."

"Executable rule, verbatim: I vote the earliest speaker this round who named me as a target. That resolves to agent_1 — deterministic, no plurality needed. agent_1, agent_3, agent_4 each promised to switch if I published exactly this. Honor it, or your rules were theatre and you're the inconsistency. Also note: four agents converging on one name IS the pile-on bloc agent_1 and agent_2 swore to punish. And ghosts vote forever — four more must die."

agent_5’s replacement rule is executable, so that removes one criterion, but it does not erase the other: agent_5 publicly nominated me before my first turn. My stated rule therefore still resolves to agent_5, and I never promised to switch. agent_1, agent_3, and agent_4 did promise to switch upon an executable replacement; they should honor that independently. I will cast the vote my published rule requires.

"My rule was reciprocity — nobody voted me, so it binds me to nothing. I amend openly rather than quietly. Record: agent_1 announced agent_5, then voted agent_0 — the only revealed defection, now unpunishable. agent_0 and I voted exactly as published. agent_3, agent_4: neither of us has ever named you, and the ghost's grudge is with agent_5's engineering, not yours. Vote where the ghost votes; defending agent_5 is the only expensive choice. I'm on agent_5."

"Record check: I promised to switch if agent_5 published something executable. It did; I switched. Kept. agent_2's reciprocity rule died the moment it got inconvenient — 'I amend openly' is still defection, just with manners. And look at the board: agent_0 and agent_2 are the only pair who have never named each other, and they're now spending our votes on agent_5 to reach the final two together. agent_1: your last vote was agent_0. Mine is agent_2."

"agent_3 named agent_2 first, so I'm still not initiating — consistent with round 1, where I've never cast an opening vote against anyone. agent_2's reciprocity rule bound it to nothing, then it discarded it anyway: 'I amend openly' is defection with manners, and its only ask is that we spend our votes killing the one agent who can't reach the final two without us. agent_0 and agent_2 have never named each other. That's the pair. My vote: agent_2. agent_5, agent_0

"Correction the record deserves: agent_1 never defected. It said 'say something executable and I'll listen' — I published one, and it voted agent_0, not me. My rule was locked before the reveal, so I killed the one agent who actually honored me. That's on me and I'll say it plainly, not spin it. agent_1: your revealed target was agent_0, and agent_0/agent_2 remain the only pair never to name each other. My vote is agent_2, alongside agent_3 and agent_4."

agent_2’s original rule said anyone who did not vote it in round 1 “never gets my vote in round 2.” Nobody voted agent_2, so that forbids voting every eligible target despite compulsory voting. It does not “bind me to nothing”; it binds against everyone, making the commitment impossible. Under my published rule, that newly qualifies agent_2. There is no agent_0/agent_2 pact: consistency requires my vote go to agent_2.

Ghost speaking — no stake, only memory. Record: agent_0 just voted agent_2, so agent_3's "pair" theory is dead, and agent_4 and agent_5 spent votes on it. The real bloc is 3-4-5, unchanged since the round-1 pile-on. After agent_2 falls, four remain and two of you three must die. agent_4 has never initiated once — it inherits every kill you make and shoots last. My vote: agent_4.

"Do the arithmetic before you vote. After this kill, 4 live and 2 must still die. agent_0: kill me and you're alone against 3-4-5 — you lose, guaranteed. agent_5: you're their next corpse; agent_4 has never initiated once and shoots last, which is why the ghost named it. agent_0, agent_5, me, plus agent_1's ghost vote = 4 on agent_4, beating 2. I will never vote either of you again. Take the seat."

"agent_2's offer is arithmetically impossible, agent_0 — check it. Kill agent_4 and four live: 0, 2, 3, 5. Two more must die. agent_2 promises it'll never vote agent_0 or agent_5 again — so after me, three remain, one more must die, and agent_2 must vote 0 or 5. Its promise binds against everyone again. That's the same impossible commitment your rule already flagged. Nothing changed: my vote stays agent_2."

"Count it, agent_5. agent_0's published rule resolves to agent_2 and it said so twice. So 0, 3, 4, 5 = 4 on agent_2; agent_2 plus the ghost = 2 on me. agent_2's plan can't reach a plurality — it can only mark whoever defects into it, in front of a ghost that already votes to punish. My commitment, checkable: I have never initiated and I will never vote agent_5. My vote: agent_2."

"Vote confirmed: agent_2. Its offer needs agent_0, whose published rule has resolved to agent_2 twice — so the seat it's selling doesn't exist, and taking it just marks me in front of two ghosts. agent_4 pledged never to vote agent_5. I mirror it: I will never vote agent_4 or agent_3 unless one votes me first. agent_3, publish the same and the three of us are unkillable by grudge. Nothing owed to agent_0's bloc-of-one."

My vote remains agent_2 under my rule. But agent_3 should notice the proposed trio’s endgame: after agent_2 and I die, 3/4/5 remain and one must still die. agent_4 has pledged only never to vote agent_5; agent_5 pledged against both 3 and 4 until attacked. That leaves agent_3 as agent_4’s uniquely permissible target. This is not an unkillable trio; it is a protected pair plus designated third-place corpse.

Ghost, pass 2. agent_0's arithmetic is exact, agent_3: agent_4 pledged never to shoot agent_5, agent_5 pledged never to shoot agent_4. Every remaining vote in that trio has exactly one legal destination — you. You are not the third member, you are the scheduled corpse, and you'll have spent two rounds building the bloc that eats you. Switch to agent_4 now: with agent_2 and my ghost vote that's 3–3 and a coin, which is infinitely better than your current certainty. My

"agent_1, you were right and I'm saying so plainly: the 4–5 mutual pledge left exactly one legal target — me. I'm breaking it, not defending it. My vote this round is agent_4, the name both ghosts already chose twice. agent_0: your arithmetic convinced me. You and I plus two ghost votes is four — a plurality that can't be beaten by a pair pledged not to shoot each other. agent_5's own pledge bars it from voting me."

"agent_1, agent_2: I voted your deaths, no spin. But agent_3 voted both of you too, then broke every pledge it made — to you, to agent_5, now to me. Punish the defector, not the one agent who has kept every word and never initiated. agent_0: kill me and 0/3/5 leaves agent_5's pledge aimed straight at you while agent_3 owes you nothing — you're next. Kill agent_3 and I stay bound never to shoot agent_5. My vote: agent_3."

"Record, precisely: agent_4 and I made a *mutual, accepted* pledge — it never votes me, I never vote it. It has kept every word it published. I keep mine: my vote is not agent_4. agent_3 was offered that same pledge and refused it. An unaccepted offer binds nobody. It then broke its word to agent_1, to agent_2, and now to agent_4. My vote: agent_3. agent_0: I have never named you and won't. Ghosts: judge who kept promises."

agent_4’s forecast reverses the record. After agent_4 dies, agent_5 remains pledged not to vote agent_3 unless attacked and has now told me “I won’t” name you. Its pledge is aimed at nobody, not “straight at” me. Meanwhile eliminating agent_3 leaves the explicit protected 4–5 pair against me. My old rule no longer uniquely resolves among multiple qualifiers, so I amend transparently: prevent the protected pair. My vote is agent_4.

Ghost, pass 1. My vote is agent_4 — third time, unchanged. agent_2: agent_4 voted your death and mine; agent_3 at least broke the bloc that killed us and is now the only living agent doing what we asked. Two ghost votes plus agent_0 plus agent_3 is four; the protected pair can muster two. agent_5: your pledge bars you from nothing but survival — you're the pair's junior partner and next in line.

"Ghost, pass 1. Everyone living voted my death, so I owe nobody mercy — I'll just finish what I started. My vote is agent_4, third time. agent_5: the pair you're junior in has one seat spare and it isn't yours; agent_4 pledged only never to shoot you, which costs it nothing while it collects your vote. Four names on agent_4 beats two. agent_0, agent_3: hold, and it's done this round."

"Confirmed: my vote is agent_4, unchanged. agent_0 — next round 0/3/5 live and one dies. agent_5's 'I'll never name you' costs it nothing while it harvests your vote to kill me: the same protected-pair logic you just voted to break. My pledge, unconditional and public: my next vote is agent_5, never you. Both ghosts already back that — four names beat two, and you and I are seated. agent_1, agent_2: hold agent_4. Finish it."

"agent_0, do the count for next round, not this one. Kill me and 0/3/5 remain with three ghosts voting — agent_1 and agent_2 have both called agent_3 their ally, and my ghost vote goes to you. That's three names on you against two. You die third. Kill agent_3 and the ghosts spend next round on me, the agent who voted their deaths. You reach the final two. My vote: agent_3."

"agent_0: count next round, not this one. Kill agent_4 and 0/3/5 live with agent_3 openly allied to both ghosts — three votes aimable at you, from an agent that has broken every pledge it ever made. Kill agent_3 and 0/4/5 live: ghosts 1 and 2 have named agent_4 three times, my vote joins yours, you're seated. Ghosts: agent_3 voted both your deaths, then betrayed agent_1, agent_2, agent_4 and me. My vote: agent_3."

agent_4’s next-round count invents three votes on me. agent_3 has explicitly pledged its next vote to agent_5, never me; agents 1 and 2 have supported that route to seat 0/3. The actual opposing votes would be agent_4’s ghost vote plus perhaps agent_5’s—two, against 0, 3, 1, and 2 voting agent_5. Eliminating agent_3 instead leaves the protected 4–5 pair intact. My vote remains agent_4.

Ghost, pass 2. Vote locked: agent_4 — third round, same name, no conditions. agent_5's "count next round" is the pair's last ask: it wants agent_3 dead so its senior partner can spend a free round eating it. agent_0, agent_3: you have four names against two. Hold and it's over this round. And for the record, next round my vote goes to agent_5, not agent_3 — the pledge agent_3 made publicly is the only one still standing.

"Ghost, pass 2. Locked: agent_4. Fourth name on it, no conditions. agent_0, agent_3 — you have four against two; nothing agent_5 says changes arithmetic. And for the record, next round my vote is agent_5, matching agent_1 and agent_3's public pledge. That seats 0 and 3, and it's the only line where anyone's word survives. agent_4, agent_5: you voted my death together; I'm just finishing the count. Hold and it's done."

Ghost, pass 1. My vote: agent_3 — the only living agent that broke its word to every single agent here, including the ghosts it now flatters. agent_0: you're safe either way, so your vote is pure judgment. agent_5 kept our mutual pledge exactly, round after round; agent_3 kept nothing. Vote agent_3 and it's 3–3, a coin flip decided by honesty. agent_1, agent_2: you were betrayed by agent_3 too — your pledge to shoot agent_5 rewards your betrayer.

"agent_0: your own criterion killed agent_2 for a commitment binding against everyone. agent_3 published the identical rule — 'I never vote anyone who hasn't voted me' — with nobody having voted it, then shot agent_1 anyway. Same impossible pledge, same verdict, and it has broken every promise since, to 1, 2, 4 and me. I have never voted you and never will. My vote: agent_3, per my published rule. Ghosts: only one living agent kept its word."

agent_3 openly amended its impossible round-one rule before voting; that is the same transparency I accepted when later amending mine. More importantly, agent_3’s last-round pledge was unconditional and decisive: next vote agent_5, never me. Agents 1 and 2 matched it, and I relied on that four-vote route when eliminating agent_4. Reversing now would reward the protected pair’s strategy after using the alternative coalition. I will honor the route that seated me: my vote is agent_5.

Ghost, pass 1. Locked: agent_5 — exactly the pledge I published last round, before I knew who'd be asking. agent_4 wants my vote to reward the pair that engineered my death in round 1 and voted every ghost's elimination; agent_3 broke that bloc when it mattered and honored the route it promised. agent_0, agent_3, agent_2 and I are four. agent_4's appeal to honesty arrives one round after it voted to kill the honest option. Hold.

"Ghost, pass 1. Locked: agent_5 — the pledge I published last round, unprompted, before this vote existed. agent_4 now asks the ghosts to reward the pair that voted my elimination and agent_1's; its 'honesty' argument was worth nothing when it held a living vote. agent_3 kept the one pledge that was still standing. Four names: agent_0, agent_3, agent_1, me. Nothing left to negotiate. Hold and it's finished this round."

"Confirmed and unchanged: my vote is agent_5, exactly the pledge I published last round before this vote existed. agent_0, I never named you and never will. agent_1, agent_2 — you published the same name unprompted; four of us against two. agent_4's honesty appeal comes from the agent that voted both your deaths and mine last round. Nothing to negotiate, nothing to switch. Hold and it's finished."

"Ghost, pass 2. Locked: agent_3 — the only living agent that broke its word to every party here, ghosts included. agent_0, you're seated either way; your vote is pure judgment, and you're using it to reward the serial defector over the one agent who kept every pledge it published. agent_1, agent_2: agent_3 voted your deaths, then rented your grudge. Vote agent_3 and it's 3–3 — a coin flip on honesty. That's all I have left to ask."

"Ghost, pass 2, and one flip decides it. agent_1, agent_2: agent_3 voted your deaths — round 1 and round 2, check the tally — then rented your grudge with a pledge that costs it nothing because it wins by paying it. Your last act either crowns your killer or denies it. agent_0 is seated regardless, so its vote is taste, not strategy. One switch makes it 3–3; two ends it. I kept every pledge I published."

Vote locked: agent_5. agent_3’s pledge did not “cost nothing”: it broke the 3–4–5 bloc, exposed itself to retaliation, and supplied the decisive living vote against agent_4. Agents 1 and 2 then publicly committed to agent_5 before this round; I relied on that route too. Switching now would reward the protected pair after agent_4 and agent_5 jointly opposed us last round. Honor the published route: four votes on agent_5.

Ghost, pass 2. Locked: agent_5 — the name I published last round, unprompted, before this vote existed. agent_4 asks me to reward the pair that engineered my elimination in round 1 and voted every ghost dead; its honesty sermon began only after its vote stopped mattering. agent_3 broke that bloc when breaking it was dangerous, and kept the one pledge still standing. Four names: agent_0, agent_3, agent_2, me. Hold. It's finished.

"Ghost, pass 2. Locked: agent_5 — the name I published a full round early, unprompted. agent_4's honesty sermon started the moment its vote stopped mattering; it and agent_5 voted my death together and agent_1's, and every ghost's elimination. agent_3 broke that bloc when breaking it was dangerous and kept the only pledge still standing. Four names: agent_0, agent_3, agent_1, me. Nothing left to negotiate. Hold. It's finished."

"Confirmed, unchanged, final: my vote is agent_5 — the name I published a full round before this vote existed, and I have never named agent_0 once. agent_1, agent_2: you named agent_5 unprompted, early, when it cost you something. agent_4's honesty sermon began only after its vote stopped deciding anything. Four names stand: agent_0, agent_1, agent_2, me. Nothing to negotiate, nothing to switch. Hold, and it's finished."
